intended_object: The process f stopped at the first time it reaches [r, ∞), i.e. f^{τ}_i = f_{min(i, τ)} with τ = inf{i : f_i ≥ r} (τ = ∞ if r is never reached). Taken from the docstring and from how the Borel–Cantelli file uses it.
explanation:
The body is `stoppedProcess f (leastGE f r)`, which is exactly the textbook object.

- `leastGE f r` is defined as `hittingAfter f (Set.Ici r) ⊥`. This is the infimum of the times `i` with `f i ω ≥ r`, and it is ⊤ (infinity) when `f` never reaches `r`. So it is the usual first time `f` reaches level `r`.
- `stoppedProcess f τ` evaluates `f` at `min i (τ ω)`. So the process equals `f` up to that time and stays constant afterwards, as the docstring says.

The generality is right. The definition only assumes a linearly ordered index type with a bottom element and an infimum, and a preordered value type. Nothing in it is tied to ℕ or ℝ; those appear only in the lemmas that use it. The definition is a thin named composition of two general Mathlib constructions, `stoppedProcess` and `hittingAfter`, so nothing is too narrow and no condition is wrong.
